working_tree_baseline: Existing changes captured by source-manifest.json, including initial-authority, policy-budget and whole-phase measurements; this review edits only its assigned JSON.

comparative_evidence.finding: SPIRE attests nodes and workloads and caches SVIDs for delivery. This supports workload identity and bounded reuse, not repeated Asservat native proofs or equivalent evidence authorization. Installing SPIRE would add infrastructure and is not recommended here.

OpenTelemetry relates an extra agent-to-gateway tier to central processing, network isolation and scale. This supports giving each physical split a concrete purpose, without removing Asservat regional or privilege boundaries.

Pyroscope v2 offers single-process evaluation/small-scale operation and recommends microservices for production at scale. This distinguishes modular code from physical deployment; it does not qualify a single-process Asservat production profile.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: These preserve documented capabilities or explicit maintainer constraints. Simplifying mechanisms must not silently remove multi-cluster operation, sharing, profiles, native files or small deployment alternatives.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Keep accepted scope and deliver through the existing slice order.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Repeated accepted-source, identity and protection proofs compound across layers; five-second or per-step cadence is engineering, not an immutable maintainer requirement.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Reuse bounded operation observations and use the authorized relaxed permission cadence, retaining effect-specific scope and original accepted operation bounds. Measure the full path, not isolated proof calls.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Guaranteeing every transient restrictive API value affects retained evidence is stronger than merely applying accepted policy revisions. The current ADR expressly requires it; this review proposes reconsideration rather than silently deleting the guarantee.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Make transient-revision semantics explicit when redesigning retention readiness; preserve all already accepted deletion obligations.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: A wildcard private-namespace guard creates controller/probe exceptions and repeated compatibility work. Native failures show real operational cost, while production attack frequency is unknown.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Retain protection from unauthorized credentialed-workload mutation; move redundant conformance proof off the request path and compare narrower admission rules before changing the boundary.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Per-download Jobs, SQL owner rendezvous and certificate-only live delivery are mechanisms, not separately accepted user capabilities. Their complete replacement is not qualified.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Remove demonstrated duplicate proof cost first; then compare reusable isolated readers and bounded permits without weakening artifact scope, cancellation or uncertain-effect accounting.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: Distinct module/SQL roles do not automatically isolate a compromised process that holds all their credentials; ADR-094 already applies this reasoning to native Pod credentials.
cross_cutting_findings.action: Consolidate same-process plumbing where justified, retaining real key, collector and hostile-parser privilege boundaries.
